title: Two layers or one in disguise?
hook: Stack two straight-line layers. Have you built something a single layer can't do?

knows: that a neural network passes values through layers
how to evaluate y = ax + b
doesNotKnow: that two straight (linear) layers in a row equal one straight layer
that a bend such as ReLU between layers is what makes depth add power

misconception: More layers always means a more powerful model.
objective: The learner can collapse two stacked straight layers into one and explain that a nonlinearity between them is needed for depth to add anything.

claims.text: The layers h = 3x + 1 and y = 2h − 5 are a toy, labelled 'Toy two-layer stack' on the stage.
claims.source: Brief 49 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md; A1, B1, A2, B2 in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: Stacked, the two layers give y = 2(3x + 1) − 5 = 6x − 3: at x = 0, 1, 2 the outputs are −3, 3, 9, all on one straight line.
claims.source: Algebra; stack(x, false) in Demo.tsx, node: −3, 3, 9 (and −9 at x = −1). A composition of affine maps is affine.

claims.text: With a ReLU between the layers (negative h becomes 0), the output is flat at −5 for x below −1/3 and follows 6x − 3 above it, a kink no single straight layer can make.
claims.source: stack(x, true) in Demo.tsx: h = 3x + 1 < 0 iff x < −1/3, then y = 2·0 − 5 = −5. node: x = −1 gives −5 (bent) vs −9 (straight).

claims.text: A nonlinearity between layers is what lets extra layers add power; real neural networks put one after each hidden layer.
claims.source: About real systems: Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016, Deep Learning §6.1 (a linear-only stack is still linear) and §6.3 (ReLU is the default hidden-unit nonlinearity); universal approximation with nonlinear activations: Cybenko 1989, Hornik 1991. 'After each hidden layer' describes standard practice, not every architecture.

recall.question: A colleague stacks ten linear layers with no activation function between them. Compared with one linear layer, the stack can represent:
options: Exactly the same straight-line maps: ten straight layers collapse into one
recall.why: Each straight layer applied to a straight layer gives another straight layer, however many you stack. A nonlinearity between them is what adds power.
